analysis: Examined the three changed files. Darkbloom.swift:60 (head) registers a new `Waitlist` subcommand. Its implementation is not in this batch, so its network calls, token use (A-008), and output handling are unverified. SandboxCommand.swift:28-31 (head) changes only the help text, which now mentions `waitlist sandbox`; no behavior changes. ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift:116 (head) adds a gate, requireNewPairApproval, before onboarding; lines 137-159 define clusterWaitlistGate and requireNewPairApproval. The gate is skipped for `.localOnly` scope and for a Mac that already holds a pairing or whose pairing cannot be read (`ClusterPairSummary.local().paired`). The gate asks via SandboxTerminal.confirm and uses FeatureWaitlistAccess.live(configPath:). This is a client-side UX gate on the owner's own CLI. Authorization for serving is platform-owned (TB-011, A-016), so bypassing it locally is expected for ADV-001 and is not a regression, provided the coordinator enforces cluster/sandbox approval server-side; that is unverified here. The pairing summary reportedly treats an unreadable pairing as paired, which fails open. This is acceptable only if the waitlist is not a security control. The gate runs before ClusterOnboardingOperations.live and before the instance lock, so a refusal leaves no partial state. Questions for integration: (1) Waitlist command and FeatureWaitlistGate/FeatureWaitlistAccess: where and how they send credentials, and the coordinator URL they use (they should honor the config's coordinator and not leak the token to an arbitrary URL). (2) Whether the coordinator enforces approval for cluster serving and sandbox setup, rather than relying on the CLI. (3) Whether the TB-013 sandbox setup path now consults the waitlist, and whether that changes trust in the installer download (T-061). No threat-model asset is weakened by the visible changes.
